# Changelog — Store

## 0.16.1

- DevQuake staff find the NPS point packages under Marketing, next to Promotions and Newsletters.

## 0.16.0

- Claims: DevQuake can give a member something to claim, such as a challenge prize. They get an
  email with a link and a secret code; signed in as themselves, they type the code and it is
  theirs. Five wrong codes lock it, and it can be claimed for 90 days.
- For now a claim gives DevQuake NPS points: DevQuake's staff keep NPS point packages in their
  shop. The packages are never shown in the shop or sold, because NPS points cannot be bought.

## 0.15.0

- The shop can show what the DevQuake art gallery is: members’ digital art, some of which may in time become designs for DevQuake products, always with the artist’s consent and under terms agreed with them. It appears above “Made by DevQuake” once switched on.

## 0.14.2

- Order and newsletter emails are sent with an updated mail library that reads email addresses more strictly, closing three ways a malformed address could have reached the wrong recipient.

## 0.14.1

- The payment keys in the shop’s payment settings no longer make the browser offer to save them as passwords.

## 0.14.0

- Tips on every page: how to see the details, how to add and how to change. Turn them on or off with 💡 at the top; the choice is kept on this device.

## 0.13.1

- Buttons that cannot be used right now show the normal arrow instead of a “forbidden” sign.

## 0.13.0

- The app is now also in Italian and Spanish: pick the language at the top of the page (in the shop, buyers find it at the bottom).

## 0.12.2

- Signing in on DevQuake with another account now also changes who you are in the shop: the shop no longer keeps the previous account’s session in another tab, and signing out of DevQuake signs you out of an account connected to it.

## 0.12.1

- The way back to DevQuake is now a small button with the DevQuake logo at the right end of the shop’s header, after the cart; hover it to see which page it returns to.

## 0.12.0

- Signed in to the shop: the newsletter is one checkbox for the email address your account already has, on your account page, in the footer and on the newsletter page. It switches on or off at once and says so, with no address to type and no confirmation email. Visitors who are not signed in still sign up with their email address.

## 0.11.0

- Signed in on DevQuake: your account in the shop shows your name and email address from DevQuake (change them there), with counters of your favourites, purchases and cart items that open each list. Your delivery details stay in the shop. The newsletter is set in your DevQuake account, so the shop no longer asks you to sign up again. Without DevQuake, the account page is as before.

## 0.10.0

- Signed in on DevQuake: once you have allowed the shop to use your sign-in address, you are signed in to the shop automatically on every visit, and its header shows your name instead of “Account”. Signing out of the shop keeps you signed out.
- Came from a DevQuake page (the platform, an app or the blog)? “← Back” at the top of the shop returns you there.

## 0.9.0

- Favourites: save products with the heart on their page and find them under Favourites in the shop’s header, with the date you saved each one, today’s price and how much cheaper or dearer it is since then. Products that can no longer be bought are struck through.
- The currency choice moved to the shop’s header, before your account and the cart.
- Customers, for the owner and the team: every buyer account and the members who voted or saved favourites, with their orders, reviews, votes, favourites and conversations, and whether each was answered or resolved. The owner and managers can block an account or delete it.

## 0.8.0

- Your shop’s logo is now the icon in the browser tab and on the home screen, on the shop’s pages and on your own pages (overview, products, orders…). Without a logo, the app’s icon stays.

## 0.7.0

- Shops that keep DevQuake’s look have a theme switch in their header: adaptive (follows your device), light or dark. Your choice also applies on DevQuake. Shops with their own design keep their colours.

## 0.6.0

- Buyers can choose a currency at the bottom of the shop and see approximate prices in it next to the real ones, at the European Central Bank’s daily rates; Romanian and Hungarian pages start with lei and forint. Orders and payments stay in the shop’s currency, and the shop says so.

## 0.5.0

- Interest votes: a product can show a vote instead of a price. Signed-in people say whether they would buy it, what they would pay and which colour, size or version they want, and can change or take back their vote.
- Statistics shows every voted product's demand, what voters would pay, a suggested price, the expected buyers, revenue, profit, return on investment and break-even, with a short verdict and the most wanted versions.
- Each product's page takes a cost per piece and a one-time investment for these estimates.

## 0.4.0

- DevQuake members continue with their DevQuake account: their account in the shop is filled in from their profile (name and email address, allowed once on DevQuake), and the shop recognises them on their next visits. Everyone else still signs up with any email address.
- Buyers save their delivery details in their account, and the checkout fills them in; at checkout they can keep new details for next time.
- The site's administrators decide whether members may open their own shops; when they may not, members see the shop like visitors.
- Optionally, visitors see what DevQuake offers and how to join, above the shop footer.
- Search engines may read the shops' pages and products and find their sitemap.

## 0.3.0

- Team members can have several roles: products, marketing, support, shipping and delivery, maintenance or manager.
- The Overview shows each member the tasks of their roles: orders to ship (mark them shipped in one click), unanswered messages and reviews to publish, sold-out and low-stock products, running campaigns and newsletters, and what the shop still lacks.
- Automatic discounts and free shipping: from an amount spent or a number of items in the cart. Buyers see the discount in the cart and at checkout, with how much is missing for the next step.
- Maintenance mode: buyers see your message instead of the shop until you switch it off.
- Your shop in any language: copy the labels buyers see, translate them, paste them back, and buyers choose the language at the bottom of the shop.

## 0.2.0

- Product types with their own fields (screen size, composition, author…), with ready-made types for electronics, clothing, shoes, books, food, cosmetics, furniture, jewellery, toys, sports and handmade goods.
- Vendors and brands for your products, a product search with filters, several products changed at once, and copies of a product in one click.
- Campaigns that lower prices for a while, voucher codes at checkout, and announcements on the shop’s pages.
- Newsletters: buyers subscribe and confirm by email; you pick products on offer or new and they appear as cards in the email, with a preview and a test email.
- Reviews with stars and comments, verified purchases, your answers and your approval first.
- Buyers can open an account with a link sent by email: their orders, messages with the shop, and a confirmation email for every order.
- Products side by side in a comparison, and every product can be shared on social networks or as a QR code to print.
- Your shop’s own design: logo, banner, colours, fonts and layout, with ready-made looks.
- Search engines: titles and descriptions with a preview, a score with tips for every product, Google Analytics, Google Ads, Tag Manager, the Meta pixel or other code after the buyer agrees, and site verification for Google and Bing.
- A team with roles (manager, editor, orders), invited with a link, and statistics of sales, views and conversion for every product.

## 0.1.0

- Your own small online shop: products with options (size, colour…), photos, stock and sale prices with a start and an end.
- Buyers pay by card (Stripe), PayPal, bank transfer or cash on delivery, straight to your own accounts; they need no account and follow their order on its own page.
- Shipping zones by country with a flat rate and free shipping from an amount; add the courier and tracking number to each order.
- An email for every new order, an overview of sales and what to ship, and a checklist before you open.
- Seller details, terms of sale and returns for EU buyers, ANPC links for Romania, and shop and product pages that search engines can index.
